title: Implement OTLP exporter adapter for Tempo ingestion with dynamic batching and tenant-aware routing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a pluggable OTLP -> Tempo exporter adapter that rewrites and batches incoming OTLP trace requests into Tempo-compatible ingest payloads. The adapter must be tenant-aware (per-API-key routing and rate limits), support dynamic batching based on observed latency and throughput, and degrade gracefully to a write-through mode when buffering is constrained. This work closes the gap between our OTLP ingress and Tempo backends for customers who prefer Tempo/Tempo+Loki stacks while preserving trace sampling and critical attributes (trace.id, span.kind, service.name, user-facing tags).
acceptance_criteria: Adapter receives OTLP gRPC and HTTP/JSON payloads and emits Tempo-compatible pushes with correct trace and span IDs preserved
Dynamic batching reduces p50 tokenization latency by at least 12% for 95th percentile traffic compared to noop batching under the same load (benchmarked in staging)
Per-tenant routing honors configured tenant mappings and fallback rules (route to tempo-region-a, tempo-region-b, or hosted-legacy)
Backpressure signals (412/503) from Tempo are retried with exponential backoff and jitter; persistent failures write to a durable retry queue and emit an alert
E2E test coverage for shimming Jaeger legacy.tags into Tempo labels and for header propagation across gateway chain
Canary rollout plan defined and executed with automated rollback on error rate > 1% for 5 minutes
technical_notes: Design: adapter is implemented as a sidecar-capable service in the trace ingestion tier. It supports an internal rate-limiter per tenant and a two-layer buffer: in-memory coalescing window for low-latency batches and a disk-backed ring buffer for overload. Batching policy is based on an adaptive heuristic: max_batch_size, max_wait_ms, and a latency-target-driven shrink/expand loop using a PID controller. Translation rules include: OTLP span.attributes -> Tempo labels, jaeger.rpc.method -> http.route fallback, and legacy jaeger.tags mapping for older customers. The adapter exposes Prometheus metrics and an admin endpoint for queue inspection.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: Ticket created and initial design doc linked; assigned to Liam
2025-02-18: Spike completed — prototype batcher that aggregates OTLP protobuf and emits Tempo JSON; microbench shows 18% CPU increase under batch window=10ms
2025-02-20: Design review with platform infra; decided to use disk-backed ring buffer (BoltDB) for persistent retry rather than S3 to meet latency goals
2025-02-28: Integration tests added; found header propagation loss when gateway strips traceparent — added preserve-headers flag
2025-03-04: Load test in staging revealed backpressure thrashing at 10k rps; tuning PID constants and increasing default max_buffer_size to mitigate
2025-03-05: Preparing canary run and runbook; pending security review for tenant routing config UI
review_feedback: Platform eng: ensure RBAC checks on tenant mapping updates; prefer k/v config in control plane rather than file-based
SRE: emit per-tenant drop counters and queue_length_histogram for alerting; add a safemode that bypasses batching when disk I/O is saturated
Security: audit KMS use for persisted retry payloads; sanitize PII in span attributes before durable write
alerting: Alert if tempo_adapter.per_tenant_drops > 100/min for any tenant
Pager if error_rate > 1% sustained for 5m during canary
notes_on_rollout: Rollout via feature flag gate at the ingress layer. Start with internal tenants in us-west-2 at 5% traffic, expand to 25% after 1 hour of stable metrics, then to 100% if no regression. Canary includes automatic rollback when error thresholds exceeded. Post-rollout: run two-week perf sweep and collect model-app traces for sampling calibration.
